mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate above 12% triggers a negative signal for S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as high unemployment indicates a weakening labor market and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of instances when the unemployment rate exceeds 12%, despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the housing starts series (HOUST) and the retail sales series (RSAFS) both exhibit a 3-month moving average increase of more than 5%, it signals a strong demand environment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in HOUST and RSAFS does not lead to significantly higher 60-day forward returns compared to periods without this joint increase (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) by more than 2% over a 6-month period indicates supply chain disruptions and potential inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO declines by more than 2% over 6 months, despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increasing by more than 1% within a 3-month window signals a tightening monetary policy, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to increased borrowing costs.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS increases by more than 1% within a 3-month window, despite the negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the GDP (GDPC1) by more than 2% over a 6-month period, coupled with a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 1%, signals a strong demand environment and a healthy labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint increase in GDPC1 and decrease in UNRATE do not lead to significantly higher 60-day forward returns compared to periods without this joint movement (t-test p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs signals a strong labor market, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to increased consumer spending and confidence.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 45% of instances when PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 jobs over 3 months, despite the positive signal.

mechanism_narrative: The consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increasing by more than 3% over a 6-month period, while the industrial production index (INDPRO) remains stagnant, signals potential inflationary pressures without corresponding economic growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The combination of high CPIAUCSL growth and stagnant INDPRO does not lead to significantly lower 60-day forward returns compared to periods without this combination (t-test p > 0.1).
